content: Brimonidine is an ophthalmic medication prescribed to reduce intraocular pressure in patients with glaucoma or ocular hypertension. Glaucoma is a condition characterized by elevated pressure in the eyes, which can damage the optic nerve and lead to vision loss. Ocular hypertension refers to higher-than-normal eye pressure that has not yet caused vision loss. Brimonidine belongs to a class of drugs known as alpha-adrenergic agonists and works by decreasing the production of fluid in the eyes. Brimonidine eye drops are available as a liquid solution to be instilled into the eyes. Typically, the drops are applied to the affected eye(s) three times daily, spaced approximately eight hours apart. It is important to use the medication at the same times each day. Follow the instructions on your prescription label carefully, and consult your doctor or pharmacist if you have any questions. Use the drops exactly as directed, without increasing or decreasing the dose or frequency unless instructed by your doctor. While brimonidine can help manage your condition, it does not cure it. Continue using the medication even if you feel well, and do not stop without consulting your doctor. To properly instill the eye drops, follow these steps: 1. Wash your hands thoroughly with soap and water. 2. Inspect the dropper tip to ensure it is not chipped or cracked. 3. Avoid touching the dropper tip to your eye or any other surface to maintain cleanliness. 4. Tilt your head back and use your index finger to gently pull down the lower eyelid, creating a small pocket. 5. Hold the dropper close to your eye without touching it, and brace the remaining fingers of that hand against your face. 6. While looking upward, gently squeeze the dropper to release one drop into the pocket formed by the lower eyelid. Then, remove your finger from the eyelid. 7. Close your eye for 2 to 3 minutes and tilt your head downward as if looking at the floor. Avoid blinking or squeezing your eyelids. 8. Apply gentle pressure to the tear duct with a finger. 9. Wipe away any excess liquid from your face with a tissue. 10. If you need to instill more than one drop in the same eye, wait at least 5 minutes before applying the next drop. 11. Replace and tighten the cap on the dropper bottle. Do not wipe or rinse the dropper tip. 12. Wash your hands again to remove any residual medication. If you miss a dose, instill it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Do not double the dose to make up for a missed one. Before using brimonidine eye drops, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to brimonidine or any other medications. Do not use brimonidine if you are taking monoamine oxidase (MAO) inhibitors, such as isocarboxazid, phenelzine, selegiline, or tranylcypromine. Provide your doctor and pharmacist with a complete list of all prescription and nonprescription medications, vitamins, supplements, and herbal products you are taking or plan to take. This includes antidepressants, barbiturates, medications for anxiety, high blood pressure, mental illness, pain, or seizures, as well as sedatives, sleeping pills, and tranquilizers. Your doctor may need to adjust your medication doses or monitor you for side effects. If you are using other topical eye medications, instill them either 5 minutes before or 5 minutes after applying brimonidine. Inform your doctor if you experience dizziness when standing up, or if you have a history of depression, circulatory conditions (e.g., Raynaud's disease or thromboangiitis obliterans), heart, kidney, or liver disease. Notify your doctor if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. If you become pregnant while using brimonidine, contact your doctor immediately. Do not breastfeed while using this medication. If you are scheduled for surgery, including dental procedures, inform your doctor or dentist that you are using brimonidine. Be aware that brimonidine may cause drowsiness and temporary blurred vision after application. Avoid driving or operating machinery until you know how the medication affects you. Consult your doctor about the safe use of alcohol while using brimonidine, as alcohol can exacerbate drowsiness caused by the medication. If you wear soft contact lenses, remove them before applying the drops and wait at least 15 minutes before reinserting them. Brimonidine may cause side effects. Notify your doctor if you experience any of the following symptoms, especially if they are severe or persistent: Itchy, irritated, red, stinging, or burning eyes Dry eyes Watery or runny eyes Red or swollen eyelids Sensitivity to light Blurred vision Headache Drowsiness Difficulty falling or staying asleep Dry mouth Runny nose or cold symptoms Cough Sore throat Flu-like symptoms Facial pain or pressure Heartburn Some side effects can be serious. Contact your doctor immediately if you experience: Rash Difficulty breathing Seeing specks or flashes of light Blind spots Fainting Dizziness Nausea In case of a serious side effect, you or your doctor may report it to the FDA's MedWatch Adverse Event Reporting program online or by phone. Store brimonidine in its original container, tightly closed, and out of reach of children. Keep it at room temperature, away from excess heat and moisture (not in the bathroom). Dispose of expired or unneeded medication properly, and consult your pharmacist for guidance on disposal. In case of overdose, contact your local poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. If the individual collapses or is not breathing, call 911 immediately. Keep all appointments with your doctor. Do not share your medication with others. Ask your pharmacist any questions about refilling your prescription. Maintain a written list of all medications, supplements, and vitamins you are taking, and bring it with you to doctor visits or hospital admissions. This information is also essential in emergencies.
